title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript note. It is a typescript page, page 80 of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §6.4. It was filed in cote 136 (archive number 398). The adjacent pages, which are genuine handwritten notes on derived functors and on Hom/⊗ of k-modules into a k-linear category, are unrelated.

Setting: S is a henselian (strictly henselian for (a)) DVR with fraction field K and residue field k of characteristic p. A is an abelian variety over K, with inertia group I in π = Gal(K^sep/K).

What 4.3 a) established, for ℓ ≠ p: the function g ↦ Tr(g | T_ℓ(A_K)) on I is integer-valued and independent of ℓ. This follows from the semistable reduction theorem: an open subgroup I' acts unipotently, and on the quotient Γ = I/I' one has the Néron model filtration (fixed / toric / abelian / toric-dual).

Use for the conductor (4.5, 4.6.2): when k is perfect, the conductor exponent of A equals the scalar product on Γ of this trace function with the Artin character. This is the Serre–Tate / Ogg type formula, conductor = tame part + Swan part.

What 4.3 b) established, for k finite: on π' (elements whose image in π_0 = Gal(k^sep/k) is an integral power of Frobenius f_q) the trace function is ℚ-valued and independent of ℓ.

Claim of 6.4: both functions can also be recovered from T_p(A_K), at least in mixed characteristic for now.

Method:
- Use the filtration (6.3.1) of the p-divisible group of A (or of its Néron model). Its three graded quotients are p-Barsotti–Tate groups Y over K with 'essentially good reduction' over S (made precise in 6.5).
- For case a), extend the residue field so that k is perfect, even algebraically closed (EGA 0_III 10.3.1).
- Choose a finite Galois extension K'/K, with group G, such that Y_{K'} has good reduction. This gives a BT group Y_{S'} over S' with a G-action compatible with the action of G on S'.
- The continuation (next typescript page, not shown) lets G act on the special fibre over k'. Through its Dieudonné module it defines a trace that recovers the required function.

This is the p-adic analogue of ℓ-independence, i.e. a precursor of the 'mysterious functor' and of Fontaine's D_pst / Weil–Deligne representation attached to T_p.
errors: No mathematical error. The restriction to unequal characteristic is explicitly flagged by Grothendieck himself ('pour le moment').
'Barsoti-Tate' (first occurrence) is a typo in the original typescript; it is spelled 'Barsotti-Tate' a few lines later.

ideas.what: The trace of inertia on T_ℓ(A) is integer-valued and independent of ℓ, and gives the conductor via a scalar product with the Artin character.
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-independence of inertia traces; Ogg–Shafarevich/Serre–Tate conductor formula

ideas.what: Recovering the same trace function from T_p via the Néron filtration of the p-divisible group, potentially good reduction of the graded pieces, and the G-action on the special fibre / Dieudonné module.
ideas.modern_name: ℓ = p independence via Dieudonné / Fontaine theory (D_pst, Weil–Deligne representation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA 7 IX §6; later Fontaine, Coleman–Iovita, Breuil, Ochiai, among others

ideas.what: Reduction to a perfect or algebraically closed residue field by residual extension.
ideas.modern_name: Residue field extension of a DVR

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exp. IX §6.4, misfiled among manuscript notes on divided-power de Rham complexes. Its content (p-adic recovery of ℓ-independent inertia traces) is published and well known as a precursor of Fontaine's theory.
transcription_corrections: The page is the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, p. 80 (§6.4), not a handwritten note. The numbers '398' and '273' are archive foliation.
π^! is probably π' (a prime with a typewriter artefact); the subgroup of π mapping to integral powers of Frobenius f_q.
Handwritten marks ('R-ꟻ' at the top, a circled 'w' and '+' near 'se ramène', and a mark at the bottom) are later editorial annotations, not part of the text.
